# Jubilees Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram Travels; Egypt; War and Rescue; Melchizedek; Hagar

---

**13:1** Abram moved south, came to Hebron — newly built at that time — and settled there for two years. Then he pushed further south to Bealoth, where he ran into a famine.

**13:2** In the third year of that week, Abram went down to Egypt and lived there five years — right up until his wife was taken from him.

**13:3** Tanis in Egypt had been built around that time, about seven years after Hebron.

**13:4** When Pharaoh kidnapped Sarai, Abram's wife, the LORD struck Pharaoh and his whole household with devastating plagues — all because of Sarai.

**13:5** By then Abram had become extraordinarily wealthy: silver, gold, cattle, donkeys, horses, camels, servants — vast riches.

**13:6** Lot had done well for himself too — his own flocks, cattle, and donkeys.

**13:7** Abram brought his wife back from Egypt and returned to where he had originally camped, between Bethel and Ai.

**13:8** After a while they parted ways: Lot took the lowland, and Abram stayed in the hills.

**13:9** Lot settled in Sodom — a city of deeply wicked people.

**13:10** It hurt Abram deeply that his nephew had left him. He had no children of his own.

**13:11** In the year Lot was captured — the fourth year of that week, just after they had separated — the LORD spoke to Abram: "Look around from where you're standing. Look north, south, east, west."

**13:12** "Every bit of land you can see — I'm giving it to you and your descendants, forever. I'll make your descendants so numerous they can't be counted, like the grains of sand on a beach."

**13:13** "Now get up and walk the whole thing — length and breadth — and take it in. Because I'm giving it to your descendants."

**13:14** Abram went and settled in Hebron.

**13:15** In the thirteenth year of the third week of this jubilee, four kings went to war against five. The five lost, and Lot was captured along with all of Sodom's possessions.

**13:16** A survivor escaped and ran to tell Abram that his nephew Lot had been taken prisoner.

**13:17** Abram mobilized his household guard — three hundred and eighteen men — and went after the kings.

**13:18** He hit them at night, chased them to Dan, cut them down. He took back everything — all the plunder and his nephew Lot.

**13:19** The king of Sodom came and bowed to Abram: "Lord Abram, give us back our people — keep the goods for yourself."

**13:20** Abram said: "I swear by the LORD God Most High, maker of heaven and earth — I will not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap from you. I won't have you saying that you made me rich."

**13:21** "The only exception: what my men have already eaten, and the share for the allies who came with me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their cut."

**13:22** Then Abram gave a tenth of all the prime spoils to Melchizedek. Melchizedek ate and drank with him.

**13:23** Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He blessed Abram: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Lord of heaven and earth."

**13:24** "And blessed be God Most High, who handed your enemies over to you."

**13:25** And Abram gave him a tenth of all he had.

**13:26** During this jubilee Abram spent thirty-five years in Canaan. Then in the sixth week, second year, Abram took Hagar as an additional wife.

**13:27** Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar — her Egyptian maidservant — and gave her to Abram as a wife.

**13:28** In the fifth year of the sixth week, Hagar bore Abram a son: Ishmael.

---
*PNEUMA notes: "Thirty-five years" renders "five weeks of years" (v.26) transparently. The Melchizedek tithe scene (vv.22-25) is given its full drama. The double reference to the tithe (vv.22 and 25) follows the text and may be a liturgical repetition.*
